newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Sun Microsystems opens Israel R&D centre.
newsitem.headline: Sun Microsystems opens Israel R&D centre.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc said on Sunday it had opened a research and development center in Israel that would develop Java software that could convert an ordinary personal computer into a network computer.
"This is the first venture of this kind for JavaSoft outside the U.S.," said Nancy Yavne, who will head the new centre.
JavaSoft is the Sun unit developing Java, software that supports network applications and enables developers to write applications that can run on any Java-enabled PC.
Yavne said the centre had six engineeres on staff and would expand the number to 15 by the end of the year and 30 after three years.

"It's easier to find engineers here than in California," she said, explaining the company's decision to set up an R&D centre in Israel. "Per capita, there are more engineers here than anywhere else in the world."
The centre will be developing JavaPC, software than converts older PCs into network computers, as well as Java security software. Sun said JavaPC would be commercially available from this fall.
